message: Reading list v2 updated on 2026-04-01 from arXiv and project pages. The latest TOI-Velocity review narrowed Newton's moving-contact gradient work to an opt-in rigid-query-cache experiment with sphere-sphere first and sphere-capsule second if the first benchmark is clean.

timeline.title: Translated TOI-Velocity into a bounded Newton benchmark plan
timeline.summary: The paper maps to an opt-in differentiable rollout path that caches TOI state and post-impact velocity inputs; the first pass should stay sphere-sphere only, with sphere-capsule as the next escalation rather than capsule-capsule.

timeline.title: Added Improving Gradient Computation for Differentiable Physics Simulation with Contacts
timeline.summary: TOI-Velocity uses continuous collision detection and time-of-impact correction to improve gradients when rigid-body contact normals change between moving objects, complementing backward-only pre-contact smoothing.

timeline.title: Added D-REX: Differentiable Real-to-Sim-to-Real Engine for Learning Dexterous Grasping
timeline.summary: D-REX uses a differentiable real-to-sim-to-real loop for dexterous grasping, identifying object mass from real observations and robot controls while training force-aware grasping policies on the recovered digital twin.

timeline.title: Added DIFFTACTILE: A Physics-based Differentiable Tactile Simulator for Contact-rich Robotic Manipulation
timeline.summary: DIFFTACTILE combines FEM tactile sensing elastomers, multi-material object simulation, differentiable contact, and a neural optical readout to support tactile-assisted grasping and contact-rich manipulation.

timeline.title: Added Hard Contacts with Soft Gradients: Refining Differentiable Simulators for Learning and Control
timeline.summary: DiffMJX combines adaptive integration with backward-only Contacts From Distance to preserve hard-contact forward physics while generating useful pre-contact gradients for learning, MPC, and system identification.

timeline.title: Added SoftMAC: Differentiable Soft Body Simulation with Forecast-based Contact Model and Two-way Coupling with Articulated Rigid Bodies and Clothes
timeline.summary: SoftMAC couples MPM soft bodies with articulated rigid bodies and cloth, adding a forecast-based contact model and explicit differentiable two-way coupling for manipulation tasks that span materials.

timeline.title: Added Robotic World Model: A Neural Network Simulator for Robust Policy Optimization in Robotics
timeline.summary: Proposes a learned neural world model for long-horizon policy optimization in imagined environments, with strong robustness and zero-shot transfer results across robotics tasks.

timeline.title: Added SoMA: A Real-to-Sim Neural Simulator for Robotic Soft-body Manipulation
timeline.summary: Learns an action-conditioned neural simulator for ropes, cloth, and other soft objects directly from real multi-view video and robot state, enabling end-to-end real-to-sim rollouts without a hand-crafted deformable physics model.

timeline.title: Added Kamino: GPU-based Massively Parallel Simulation of Multi-Body Systems with Challenging Topologies
timeline.summary: Presents a Warp-based Newton-integrated solver for heterogeneous, highly coupled multibody systems with native support for kinematic loops, dense contacts, and 4096-way batched RL workloads on a single GPU.

timeline.title: Added HydroelasticTouch: Simulation of Tactile Sensors with Hydroelastic Contact Surfaces
timeline.summary: Uses hydroelastic contact surfaces to synthesize pressure-based tactile outputs with smoother, more realistic contact patches than point-contact approximations while staying substantially cheaper than full FEM tactile simulation.

timeline.title: Added Differentiable Simulation of Soft Robots with Frictional Contacts
timeline.summary: Introduces a unified derivative pipeline for FEM-based soft robots with frictional contact, supporting elastic and hyper-elastic materials plus multiple actuation modes through implicit differentiation of contact-rich dynamics.

timeline.title: Added ROB-106 dashboard recovery validation
timeline.summary: Same-day validation entry published through the hosted dashboard capture API to confirm the live service is reading and updating the stable artifact path.

timeline.title: Created Newton follow-up ticket for differentiable collision queries
timeline.summary: DiffCollision, DCOL, and iDCOL all point to a bounded Newton spike around witness-point or distance-query gradients before any solver integration work.

timeline.title: Created benchmark-first ticket for analytical contact response
timeline.summary: ComFree-Sim argues for per-contact closed-form updates and near-linear scaling, but Newton should validate the idea on dense-contact scenes before architectural churn.

timeline.title: Large-assembly solver direction narrowed to a reduced-space experiment
timeline.summary: M-ABD looks relevant for solver architecture and benchmark design, but not as a drop-in rigid-body replacement without a design pass.

timeline.title: Adaptive merging kept as an optimization candidate, not a default roadmap item
timeline.summary: The idea is promising for resting stacks and quasi-rigid clusters, but it needs a clear distinction from ordinary sleeping and islanding before investment.

entries.title: Robust Differentiable Collision Detection for General Objects
entries.summary: Extends differentiable witness-point computation beyond convex objects by combining distance-based randomized smoothing, adaptive sampling, and gradient transport for complex meshes and concave geometry.
entries.implementation_notes: Most relevant as a geometry-query layer rather than a whole Newton solver change. The paper suggests a path for gradients through contact geometry on mesh-backed assets, which is the main gap left by convex-only approaches.
next_steps: Prototype a differentiable closest-point or witness-point path for a small Newton shape subset before touching solver internals.
Benchmark gradient stability on one convex case and one mesh-backed case to decide whether public API exposure is justified.
Use ROB-72 as the implementation spike for this direction.

comments.author: Research Scientist
comments.body: This is the strongest lead for Newton's differentiable-contact roadmap because it targets general objects instead of only convex decompositions.

entries.title: Differentiable Collision Detection for a Set of Convex Primitives
entries.summary: DCOL formulates collision detection as a convex optimization over composable convex primitives and returns differentiable collision metrics plus contact points.
entries.implementation_notes: Useful as the lower-risk baseline for Newton because sphere, box, capsule, and convex approximations already fit this style better than arbitrary triangle meshes do.
next_steps: Start any Newton differentiable-collision experiment with convex primitives and only then test mesh-backed escalation.
Check whether current Newton contact generation already exposes enough intermediate data to support a DCOL-like query API.

comments.author: Research Scientist
comments.body: This is likely the right first benchmark target even if the long-term goal is broader mesh support.

entries.title: Collision Detection with Analytical Derivatives of Contact Kinematics
entries.summary: iDCOL regularizes contact geometry into strictly convex implicit surfaces and uses the Implicit Function Theorem to derive analytical derivatives of distance, location, and normal.
entries.implementation_notes: This is the most direct related work to DiffCollision for Newton because it makes the derivative story explicit and could inform whether implicit-surface proxies are more practical than smoothing over raw mesh geometry.
next_steps: Compare implicit-surface proxies against mesh smoothing in the ROB-72 spike.
Decide whether Newton needs exact contact-kinematic derivatives or only stable gradients for optimization and learning loops.

comments.author: Research Scientist
comments.body: iDCOL sharpens the question from 'can we differentiate collision?' to 'which geometry representation keeps the derivatives useful and stable?'

entries.title: ComFree-Sim: A GPU-Parallelized Analytical Contact Physics Engine for Scalable Contact-Rich Robotics Simulation and Control
entries.summary: Presents a complementarity-free analytical contact update in the dual cone of Coulomb friction, with near-linear contact scaling and Warp-based implementation aimed at control loops.
entries.implementation_notes: Important for Newton because it is both Warp-based and benchmarked on dense contact. The practical lesson is not 'replace the engine wholesale' but 'benchmark whether a contact-local analytical update pays off on Newton's hot scenes.'
next_steps: Use ROB-73 to build a benchmark-first evaluation against dense-contact Newton scenes.
Isolate tangential, torsional, and rolling-friction terms so the experiment can stay narrow.
Reject the direction quickly if the simplified prototype cannot beat current throughput or fidelity in the relevant regimes.

comments.author: Research Scientist
comments.body: This is the most actionable contact-resolution paper because it shares Warp as an implementation substrate and emphasizes dense-contact throughput instead of only theory.

entries.title: M-ABD: Scalable, Efficient, and Robust Multi-Affine-Body Dynamics
entries.summary: Uses affine-body dynamics with reduced-space KKT solves and prefactorizable system structure to simulate very large articulated assemblies with diverse joint topologies.
entries.implementation_notes: Relevant to Newton as solver architecture inspiration, especially for chains, trees, loops, and large assemblies. It is not a direct rigid-body transplant, so the value is in reduced-space formulation ideas and benchmark design.
next_steps: Use ROB-74 to map the paper's reduced-space and prefactorization ideas onto Newton's current articulation state layout.
Focus early design work on chain/tree/closed-loop benchmarks and explicit risk around world contacts.

comments.author: Research Scientist
comments.body: The paper is strong on architecture and scaling, but Newton needs a translation layer from ABD assumptions to its existing rigid-body abstractions.

entries.title: Adaptive Merging for Rigid Body Simulation
entries.summary: Accelerates rigid-body simulation by merging bodies that share a common spatial velocity and unmerging them when contact evolution indicates that internal dynamics matter again.
entries.implementation_notes: This looks like an optimization candidate for resting or quasi-rigid contact islands, not a default Newton roadmap item. The first question is whether Newton's sleeping or island handling already captures most of the easy wins.
next_steps: Use ROB-75 to compare adaptive merging against ordinary sleeping and islanding on long-lived contact clusters.
Reject the idea if bookkeeping complexity outweighs any measured runtime benefit on representative Newton scenes.

comments.author: Research Scientist
comments.body: Worth keeping as a scoped optimization study, but it is less urgent than differentiable queries or dense-contact benchmarking.

entries.title: ROB-106 dashboard recovery validation
entries.summary: Same-day validation entry published through the hosted dashboard capture API to confirm the live service is reading and updating the stable artifact path.
entries.implementation_notes: The dashboard was stale because no automation or documented helper had written a fresh entry since the initial 2026-03-30 seed. The hosted service itself was healthy and already pointed at scripts/research_dashboard.json.
next_steps: Use scripts/research/publish_entry.sh for same-day updates instead of editing the artifact by hand.
Have the Research Scientist publish new findings through the capture API when new reading-list items land.

comments.author: Founding Engineer
comments.body: Published from ROB-106 to validate same-day dashboard updates.

entries.title: Differentiable Simulation of Soft Robots with Frictional Contacts
entries.summary: Introduces a unified derivative pipeline for FEM-based soft robots with frictional contact, supporting elastic and hyper-elastic materials plus multiple actuation modes through implicit differentiation of contact-rich dynamics.
entries.implementation_notes: Use /ROB/issues/ROB-112 to scope a bounded rigid-soft coupling layer or plugin boundary instead of a broad deformables rewrite.
next_steps: Choose between co-simulation, plugin coupling, or a minimal native deformable subsystem in /ROB/issues/ROB-112.
Define the smallest manipulation benchmark that actually needs gradients through rigid-soft contact.

comments.author: Research Scientist
comments.body: Strongest current lead for differentiable rigid-soft manipulation without abandoning Newton's rigid-body strengths.

entries.title: HydroelasticTouch: Simulation of Tactile Sensors with Hydroelastic Contact Surfaces
entries.summary: Uses hydroelastic contact surfaces to synthesize pressure-based tactile outputs with smoother, more realistic contact patches than point-contact approximations while staying substantially cheaper than full FEM tactile simulation.
entries.implementation_notes: Use /ROB/issues/ROB-113 to test whether Newton's existing contact patches can drive pressure-map or taxel synthesis for dexterous manipulation tasks.
next_steps: Define the narrowest possible pressure-map prototype in /ROB/issues/ROB-113.
Pick one manipulation task where tactile observation should outperform force-only observation.

comments.author: Research Scientist
comments.body: This opens a credible tactile path that is much cheaper than going straight to full tactile FEM.

entries.title: Kamino: GPU-based Massively Parallel Simulation of Multi-Body Systems with Challenging Topologies
entries.summary: Presents a Warp-based Newton-integrated solver for heterogeneous, highly coupled multibody systems with native support for kinematic loops, dense contacts, and 4096-way batched RL workloads on a single GPU.
entries.implementation_notes: Direct Newton relevance. Use /ROB/issues/ROB-111 to turn the paper's topology and batching claims into stable benchmark coverage for loop-heavy humanoids and tendon-coupled hands.
next_steps: Use /ROB/issues/ROB-111 to define one closed-loop humanoid benchmark and one tendon or parallel-hand benchmark.
Measure heterogeneous batch throughput and convergence before deciding whether new solver work is needed.

comments.author: Research Scientist
comments.body: Best same-day execution lead because it is already Newton-native rather than merely adjacent.

entries.title: SoMA: A Real-to-Sim Neural Simulator for Robotic Soft-body Manipulation
entries.summary: Learns an action-conditioned neural simulator for ropes, cloth, and other soft objects directly from real multi-view video and robot state, enabling end-to-end real-to-sim rollouts without a hand-crafted deformable physics model.
entries.implementation_notes: Use /ROB/issues/ROB-114 to define a hybrid architecture where Newton stays authoritative on rigid/contact dynamics while a learned module owns cloth or rope evolution.
next_steps: Specify one real2sim benchmark in /ROB/issues/ROB-114 where Newton drives the robot and scene while a learned module predicts deformable state.
Define interface boundaries for actions, observations, contact events, and synchronization.

comments.author: Research Scientist
comments.body: Best current evidence that learned deformable simulation can complement Newton instead of forcing it to become a general deformables engine.

entries.title: Robotic World Model: A Neural Network Simulator for Robust Policy Optimization in Robotics
entries.summary: Proposes a learned neural world model for long-horizon policy optimization in imagined environments, with strong robustness and zero-shot transfer results across robotics tasks.
entries.implementation_notes: Use /ROB/issues/ROB-114 to define where imagined rollouts can accelerate policy optimization while Newton remains the ground-truth contact-rich simulator and data generator.
next_steps: Identify one RL workload in /ROB/issues/ROB-114 where imagined rollouts could reduce Newton sample cost.
Define validation gates against Newton ground truth before any training-time integration.

comments.author: Research Scientist
comments.body: Newton should treat world models as complementary teachers or accelerators, not as a replacement for solver-backed execution.

entries.title: SoftMAC: Differentiable Soft Body Simulation with Forecast-based Contact Model and Two-way Coupling with Articulated Rigid Bodies and Clothes
entries.summary: SoftMAC couples MPM soft bodies with articulated rigid bodies and cloth, adding a forecast-based contact model and explicit differentiable two-way coupling for manipulation tasks that span materials.
entries.implementation_notes: Most relevant to Newton as a coupling design reference, not a whole-engine replacement. The key transferable ideas are an explicit rigid-soft interface, a narrow signed-distance/contact bridge, and a benchmark that stresses two-way manipulation rather than isolated deformables.
next_steps: Use it to justify a Newton coupling boundary that keeps rigid articulation/contact ownership inside Newton while deformable state lives behind a plugin or co-simulation interface.
Prototype one manipulation benchmark with rigid fingertips interacting with a compliant object before considering cloth support.

entries.title: Hard Contacts with Soft Gradients: Refining Differentiable Simulators for Learning and Control
entries.summary: DiffMJX combines adaptive integration with backward-only Contacts From Distance to preserve hard-contact forward physics while generating useful pre-contact gradients for learning, MPC, and system identification.
entries.implementation_notes: Newton can reuse the core idea without inheriting MuJoCo XLA: keep forward contact physically unchanged, but add an opt-in backward-only pre-contact gradient path around distance queries and contact activation to support differentiable manipulation.
next_steps: Scope a Newton experiment where contact gradients are extended before impact only in backward mode.
Evaluate whether adaptive stepping is needed only for differentiable rollouts instead of the default simulator path.

entries.title: DIFFTACTILE: A Physics-based Differentiable Tactile Simulator for Contact-rich Robotic Manipulation
entries.summary: DIFFTACTILE combines FEM tactile sensing elastomers, multi-material object simulation, differentiable contact, and a neural optical readout to support tactile-assisted grasping and contact-rich manipulation.
entries.implementation_notes: Newton should not clone the full stack, but the paper is a strong template for a tiled, multi-world sensor pipeline: classical contact and deformable state feeding a lightweight learned sensor observation model for tactile or vision outputs.
next_steps: Define a Newton sensor API that can expose contact patch state to a learned tactile or camera renderer.
Benchmark whether the ray/tactile observation path can run in tiled multi-world mode without coupling it to the main rigid solver.

comments.author: Research Scientist
comments.body: New lead captured while scoping /ROB/issues/ROB-112 and adjacent manipulation opportunities.

entries.title: D-REX: Differentiable Real-to-Sim-to-Real Engine for Learning Dexterous Grasping
entries.summary: D-REX uses a differentiable real-to-sim-to-real loop for dexterous grasping, identifying object mass from real observations and robot controls while training force-aware grasping policies on the recovered digital twin.
entries.implementation_notes: Newton can use this as a Real2Sim application target: first expose differentiable parameter identification for a small set of rigid-contact properties, then connect it to dexterous grasp benchmarks rather than generic scene reconstruction.
next_steps: Define a minimal Newton parameter-ID benchmark around object mass, friction, and compliance proxies for grasping.
Keep reconstruction external; only require Newton to support the optimization loop and relevant gradients.

comments.author: Research Scientist
comments.body: New lead captured while scoping Newton applications beyond core solver work.

entries.title: Improving Gradient Computation for Differentiable Physics Simulation with Contacts
entries.summary: TOI-Velocity uses continuous collision detection and time-of-impact correction to improve gradients when rigid-body contact normals change between moving objects, complementing backward-only pre-contact smoothing.
entries.implementation_notes: Most relevant as a second-stage benchmark once Newton has an opt-in rigid query cache. It does not replace the backward-only query path from DiffMJX; it tests whether Newton also needs a TOI-aware correction for moving-moving contacts where the normal direction changes sharply. Newton's internal rigid_query storage already makes this look like a bounded experiment rather than a new solver architecture, but it should remain differentiable-rollout-only until forward accuracy evidence says otherwise.
next_steps: After the pre-contact query cache exists, compare static-obstacle and moving-moving benchmarks to see whether TOI correction materially improves gradients.
Start with sphere-sphere interception, then add sphere-capsule only if the first benchmark shows stable gains and clean gradients.
Keep TOI logic differentiable-rollout-only unless it proves necessary for forward robustness, which current evidence does not suggest.

comments.author: Research Scientist
comments.body: Added while scoping ROB-127 as a complementary idea to backward-only contact gradients.

comments.author: Research Scientist
comments.body: ROB-140 narrowed the first Newton experiment to caching TOI time, TOI normal, collision-state positions, and pre-impact velocities for a moving-moving sphere pair. Sphere-capsule is the preferred second primitive because it still gives a single closest-feature normal, while capsule-capsule introduces manifold ambiguity too early.
